- Data retention & logging: current defaults and options for extended retention for audit purposes.

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Access controls (RBAC / support access / break-glass) — post-call recap

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Admin vs Developer vs View-only: we have ~6 platform admins, ~18 developers, and ~120 read-only product users. Will need least-privilege by default.
- Support access: For Prod, we prefer pre-approval for any direct access to customer data or debugging sessions that involve PII. For low-risk logs (service-level metrics), after-the-fact approvals are OK.
- Break-glass: must be logged, must notify our security mailbox (security@fintrust.com), and we require an auditable justification recorded in a ticket.
- Retention: audit logs need 1 year by default; we may request up to 3 years for specific endpoints.

Also can you confirm where support access sessions are logged (internal logs vs customer-visible audit)? We want assurance that we can access a copy of the support access audit for our compliance team.

I’ve attached our internal access-controls spreadsheet for reference. Can we schedule the deep-dive next Wed 4/21 at 11am PT?

Alex

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Access controls (RBAC / support access / break-glass) — answers & next steps

Alex — thanks, very helpful. Quick answers inline and next steps below.

1) RBAC roles & counts
- We support org-scoped roles: Org Admin, Project Admin, Developer, Viewer. Roles are configurable per-organization via SSO + SCIM mapping or our admin console.
- We can map your 6 admins / 18 developers / 120 view-only users into our role model; Dylan will show SCIM provisioning in the technical session.

2) Support access & break-glass
- Support access is just-in-time and time-limited by default. For Prod with PII access, we offer two modes:
  a) Pre-approved sessions: Customer approves each session (recommended for Prod PII).
  b) Break-glass flow: emergency access which requires an immediate ticket and automated notification to your security mailbox; full justification and approver details are captured afterward.
- All support sessions require an access request ticket (we can integrate with your Jira). The ticket and session transcript are stored in our audit log.
- We can provide a customer-visible audit export (CSV or direct Drive link) showing who accessed what, when, and for how long.

3) Logging & retention
- Default access-log retention: 90 days.
- Options: configurable to 1 year or 3 years for an additional retention package (we’ll include pricing in the next email).
- Logs include: user id, role, timestamp, session id, actions performed, and full session transcript for interactive support.

4) Data residency
- We support US-only production deployments (AWS us-east-1 / us-west-2). We’ll confirm region in the deployment questionnaire.

Next steps / asks from FinTrust:
- Confirm preferred support access mode for Prod (pre-approval or break-glass).
- Confirm audit retention requirement (1yr vs 3yr).
- Confirm a few candidate times for SE deep-dive — Wed 4/21 11am PT (proposed) works for us; please confirm.
- If you want, we can share a signed SOC2 copy and a short architecture diagram for the Prod deployment.

Attached: Redwood_RBAC-overview.pdf, SOC2-Attestation-2026.pdf, access-req-template.xlsx

I’ll book the SE deep-dive once you confirm time. Dylan / Dev — looping you in to prepare SCIM/SAML notes and the audit retention options.

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Access controls (RBAC / support access / break-glass) — implementation detail

Alex / Priya — quick add from the product/security side on the support access flow so you have a concrete implementation sketch before Wed’s session: 

- Support session flow (recommended default for Prod):
  1) Customer opens access request (via Jira/Drive form / API).
  2) Support engineer requests just-in-time access; request goes to customer approver (pre-approval) or is flagged as break-glass if urgent.
  3) If break-glass is used: emergency code is issued, session is time-limited to 30 minutes by default, and system triggers an automated email to security@fintrust.com plus creates a ticket in the integrated tracker.
  4) All sessions are recorded and write-protected; tamper-evident checksum is stored in the audit index.
  5) Customer-visible audit export is generated on-demand (CSV/JSON) and can be pushed to your S3 bucket or Drive folder for retention and e-discovery.

- We support SCIM provisioning for role sync and SAML for auth; role mappings can be enforced on first-login to avoid privilege creep.

I’ll bring a short runbook to the SE deep-dive that shows the Jira ticket fields and the break-glass email template.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Product Security Lead | Redwood Inference
